subject: Data residency & private deployment confirmation — Acme (hosting regions, VPC controls)
messages:
From: Maya Patel <maya.patel@acme-corp.com>
To: hannah_schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Jared Thompson <jared.thompson@acme-corp.com>, compliance@acme-corp.com
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: Confirmation of EU-only hosting and VPC deployment controls

Hannah —

Thanks for taking this. As part of Acme's procurement review we need a concise set of confirmations and evidence that Redwood can meet our EU data residency and private deployment controls for our enterprise contract. Specifically we need to confirm: 

1) Can you guarantee that customer data (inputs, outputs, KV cache, audit logs) for our instances will be stored and processed only in eu-west-1 (Ireland) for this contract?
2) For Redwood Private deployments: can Redwood run inside our AWS account (customer-managed VPC) or do we need a Redwood-managed VPC? If customer-managed, what level of peering/ENI access is required?
3) KMS and key custody: do you support BYOK with external KMS (AWS KMS imported keys or HSM)? If so, what key policies/audit trails are available?
4) Audit logs and retention: can we get a dedicated audit export (S3) with 365-day retention?

If you can provide a short written confirmation and attach SOC 2 Type II evidence + the CAIQ/SSP slices that correspond to hosting/keys/networking, that would help speed procurement. Ideally we get this before our security review next Monday (23 Nov).

Appreciate it,

Maya Patel
Head of Vendor Security | Acme Corp
[Attachment: acme-questionnaire-2026.docx]

From: hannah_schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Maya Patel <maya.patel@acme-corp.com>
Cc: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 11:08:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Confirmation of EU-only hosting and VPC deployment controls

Maya —

Thanks for the clear list. Short answers up-front, followed by attachments and a pointer to the runbook: 

1) EU processing & storage: Yes — for the Enterprise SLA we can pin your account to eu-west-1 only. All runtime inference, KV caches, artifact storage and audit logs for your tenant will be constrained to that region. We enforce region pinning at the routing layer and at deployment time; fallbacks to other regions are disabled for pinned accounts.

2) Private deployment model: We support two options: 
  - Customer-managed VPC (recommended): Redwood Private components run in your AWS account inside your VPC via CloudFormation/Terraform. We deploy worker instances into customer subnets; a small control-plane connector (e.g., bastion + outbound TLS) is used for control messages. No cross-account read access to your S3.
  - Redwood-managed VPC: for customers that want Redwood to operate networking; still region-pinned and isolation controls apply.

In the customer-managed case we require the following minimal networking: 2 private subnets for workers, an optional interface endpoint for S3 if you prefer traffic to stay on AWS backbone, and a Security Group allowing HTTPS out to our controlplane endpoint. We do not require VPC peering; we use customer-hosted ENIs and IAM roles.

3) KMS/BYOK: We support BYOK with AWS KMS and we can integrate with HSM-backed keys. You retain full KMS key control in your account; Redwood is provided encrypt/decrypt permission via a narrowly scoped IAM role and we never see plaintext keys. Audit events are logged to CloudTrail in your account.

4) Audit logs: We can deliver audit streams to your S3 bucket (encrypted with your KMS) with configurable retention; 365 days is supported. We can also provide a 90/180/365-day log export snapshot for your SOC reconciliation.

Attachments: SOC 2 Type II summary + CAIQ answers + a draft runbook for a customer-managed VPC. See the attached: "redwood-soc2-type2-2025.pdf", "caiq-responses-acme.xlsx", "acme-vpc-runbook-v1.pdf".

I copied Stephanie (sales lead) and Kimberly (legal) for any contract or control wording follow-ups. If that looks OK I can loop in Dylan (infra) with the network diagram and the specific Terraform artifacts.

Best,

Hannah Schmitt
Head of Growth — Redwood Inference

From: dylan_brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
To: Maya Patel <maya.patel@acme-corp.com>, hannah_schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 08:46:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Confirmation of EU-only hosting and VPC deployment controls

Hi Maya —

Jumping in with the engineering details that procurement/security typically asks for. I attached a network diagram and a short checklist. Key points: 

- Deployment artifacts: we provide a Terraform module that spins up the Redwood worker ASGs (mixed instances for GPU/CPU), worker IAM roles, and an S3 bucket policy that only allows access from the worker role. You keep the S3 bucket in your account and we never configure cross-account write access.

- Networking: we use customer subnets and allocate Elastic Network Interfaces (ENIs) from those subnets for worker nodes. Control-plane communications are outbound-only TLS to our control endpoint (it terminates in eu-west-1). No inbound holes are required. If you prefer a PrivateLink endpoint for control-plane traffic we can support that.

- KMS & key lifecycle: BYOK workflows supported. We supply a minimal IAM policy to grant cryptographic operations to the worker role. All cryptographic operations happen inside your account; logs appear in your CloudTrail and we can provide a signed manifest of key usage per request window.

- KV cache & runtime: ephemeral KV caches remain in-memory on worker instances and are not persisted to our central storage unless you enable long-term cache. If long-term cache is enabled it will be stored in your S3 and encrypted with your KMS.

Attachments included: "network-diagram-acme-vpc.png" and an exportable Terraform example. I also included a proposed runbook excerpt for onboarding.

If you want, we can schedule a 30-minute technical call (I can share the Terraform module and run through the CloudFormation variant).

—Dylan
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: network-diagram-acme-vpc.png (PNG, 320KB)]

This is great, thank you. The responses are exactly what the security team needs. A few quick confirmations so we can close the PR: 

• EU-only: confirmed and we'll include the region pinning language in the contract.
• Customer-managed VPC + BYOK: acceptable; security will review the Terraform module but preliminary thumbs up.
• Audit logs to our S3 with 365-day retention: confirmed.

I've attached our completed CAIQ subset for you to review (we filled in a couple of operational questions). Once you confirm the CAIQ rows we will finalize the assessment and move to legal for signature.

Thanks again — can we aim to freeze the CAIQ by EOD Tue (23 Nov)? If so I'll route to legal.
